text.title: Коротко
lines: If the Headquarters is destroyed, the attacker wins the battle, the Victory Points, and all of the resources that were at risk.
The Headquarters' own level determines the maximum level for various other buildings.
Destroying buildings on a base causes the Headquarters to take damage.
At level 13, the Headquarters gains the ability to save, rename, edit and load base layouts. This starts at two, with one more unlocking at levels 14, 16, 18 and 20 for a maximum of six layouts.

text.title: Что меняется с уровнем
lines: When starting your game, the Headquarters appears as a square structure with stone walls, a wooden roof, a small blue flag at the front corner, sandbags lying on the ground and a tripod on the roof.
At level 2, the Headquarters gains more sandbags on the ground and on the roof and crates against the wall. A small part of the roof has blue boards.
At level 3, the Headquarters gains some sandbags on its roof and its sides.
At level 4, more blue boards and sandbags are added to the roof.
At level 5, the antenna gains a top, and the front entrance gains a white outline and a wooden door.
At level 6, the roof changes entirely, becoming blue entirely except for the center. It gains a pole on top, and the three crates are replaced by one, larger crate.
At level 7, the Headquarters gains a blue corrugated metal roof, a hatch on the roof and 3 poles at the back.
At level 11, the Headquarters gains reinforced blue steel plating as a roof and a satellite dish on the top. The crate on the side of the Headquarters is now made of olive-colored metal.

At level 17, the Headquarters' satellite dish turns dark grey and becomes bigger, and it gains a signal pole. A lock appears at the front door, and hazard tape is on its bottom. The crate is replaced by 3 orange tubes. A second, smaller floor is added, as evidenced by the windows. The windows on the side are removed.

At level 21, the Headquarters becomes taller, gains a new front structure with a second satellite dish, gains new red vents on both sides, and the three orange tubes as well as the sandbags are removed.

At level 22, the Headquarters' satellite dish turns from being spherical to parabolic. Hazard tape can be found near the edges of the satellite dish. The door turns red, and the front of the HQ is reinforced further.

At level 23, the Headquarters gains some sandbags around the HQ. Its door is reinforced with a vault like lock. The satellite disk turns back into a round disk, with its shape sort of like a level 6-8 radar, but with a red body. What can be assumed to be generators or pipes are sheltered by a steel protrusion to the side of the building.

At level 24, the Headquarters gains a second radar on top of its left ceiling. The lock gains outer red balls on the handles. The sandbags are replaced with concrete barriers. The antennas are unified into a single pole with a red receiver. The ceiling on top of the door now has a red plate covering it. The power generator on the side becomes more advanced with a blue cover and four metal plates. Some edges and sides become gray.

At level 25, the Headquarters' base has been reinforced with Dragon's Teeth in lieu of concrete barriers. Most blue portions of the building gained darker accents, with the vault door now having a circular handle instead, topped by an unknown tiny apparatus. The two smaller radars dishes are consolidated into one with two antennae, and the chimney has been upgraded with a robust ventilation network, complete with a red-trimmed grated exit and two additional pipes.

text.title: Интересное
lines: There are special requirements, apart from XP level alone, required to upgrade your HQ up to level 8:
To upgrade your HQ to level 4, you need to build the Radar.
Similarly, the Radar must be upgraded to level 2 in order to upgrade the HQ to level 5.
To upgrade your HQ to level 6, you must have at least one troop upgraded to level 2.
To upgrade your HQ to level 7, you must have at least one Landing Craft upgraded to level 4.
To upgrade your HQ to level 8, you need to build the Sculptor.

A player's Headquarters can have up to 12,947,200 health, barring any boosts from Tribes. To reach this number, the player would require a level 29 Headquarters, 5 Mark III Shield Generators, the best Building Health Masterpiece (32%), and 12 of the best Building Health Guardians (13%), all boosted. The health can be increased with the HQ Lifepoint Tribe Boost, which can have one of the following two maximum percentages:
With the maxed HQ Lifepoint Tribe Boost (75%), the HQ can have up to 14,987,200 health.
With the maxed HQ Lifepoint Tribe Boost (100%), the HQ can have up to 15,667,200 health.
With the maxed HQ Lifepoint Tribe Boost (150%), the HQ can have up to 17,027,200 health.
When the player attacks either by landing troops or using Gunboat Weaponry, all of the Blackguard villagers will rush into the HQ to hide.

If you destroy the HQ right after a Mortar (or any other defense in general) fires, your troops can still be damaged or destroyed by the lingering projectile. This has no effect on the outcome of the battle, such as losing your last troops to said projectile will still result in a victory rather than a defeat.
If you watch a replay of an attack on one of Lt. Hammerman's bases, the Headquarters will appear as a normal Blackguard one.
https://boombeach.fandom.com/wiki/File:Everspark_HQ_Hack.mp4There's an achievement which is called Chain of Command that gives a total of 60 diamonds upon upgrading the Headquarters to level 20.

text.title: Коротко
lines: The Landing Craft trains troops for deployment, and acts as a rendezvous point during retreats.
When landed on a beach, the game places a flag at the targeted point. Assuming a Flare is not used, loaded troops will move to where the flag is before walking to the nearest building.
During Beta troops has their own flag color.
Rifleman had blue flags, Heavies had green flags, Zookas had purple flags and Warriors/Tanks had red flags. The Medic's Flag Color is unknown.
This was removed in an unknown update, so your troops always have blue and enemies always have red flags.

Each Landing Craft has a limited capacity and holds only one type of troop. Any excess space will go unused if it cannot accommodate additional units. This, in turn, determines the total loading time and cost.
They cannot be reinforced with additional troops during upgrades, but otherwise function normally.
Heroes do not take up any space in Landing Crafts, as they have their own, which allow for the deployment of only one Hero per battle.

text.title: Что меняется с уровнем
lines: Each time the Landing Craft is upgraded, the white number on the rear of the craft increases by one (up to level 22). This number corresponds to the total troop capacity of the Landing Craft. Also, its body becomes a bit longer.
Initially, the Landing Craft is a platform with blue sides, a ramp, and a cabin with a flag, hatch, and light on it.
At level 8, the Landing Craft's hatch grows taller and changes color, the light grows longer, and the sides of the Landing Craft gain pipes that run down them.

At level 15, the Landing Craft is transformed into a lighter-colored hovercraft, as indicated by the black skirt protruding from the bottom and the pair of added propellers on the rear of the craft. Also the Landing Craft's hatch grows taller.

At level 21, the Landing Craft gains dark gray sides and reverts to a platform following the removal of the black skirts from level 15-20 Landing Crafts; however, the propellers change from being fan-shaped to resemble that of a jet. Also, the ramp gains a caution design on the end of it. The flag on the rear of the craft is also removed.
At level 22, the jet-like propellers turn from blue to black. The metal plates at the back become bigger, and sport caution designs on their perimeters.

text.title: Интересное
lines: The troop capacity of a Landing Craft is equal to its level +4, and a Rifleman takes up one space so a Landing Craft's troop capacity is also equal to the number of Riflemen the Landing Craft can hold.
At levels 1-14, Landing Crafts resemble the WWII-era LCVP.
The level 15-20 Landing Crafts appear to be inspired by the LCACs
If an island has 2 landing zones and all of your Landing Craft do not fit on one of them, the remaining Landing Crafts will always be deployed in the other landing zone.
Apart from its level 2 upgrade, the Landing Craft’s maximum level is also directly determined by the Headquarters — except at HQ level 27, where the Landing Craft receive no new level.

The troops on a Landing Craft face the rear of the craft when in dock. Foot troops could easily board and then turn about-face, but mechanized units like Tanks would be reversed on so that they faced the correct direction, as they could not rotate once loaded.
The light indicator on the rear of the Landing Craft glows red when empty/half-full, yellow when training troops, and green when filled with troops.
Despite being flying units, Rocket Choppas and Heavy Choppas are still deployed with them, as with any other troop.
Unlike other buildings, a landing craft cannot swap places with another landing craft during upgrade.
Interestingly, if you retreat, troops on the landing craft can still be stunned, even if it has no effect.
This also happens if the landing craft is stunned at the beginning of an attack.

If due to a bug/exploit a tree or rock is placed right where troops exit from the Landing Craft, due to obstacles having collision and being indistructible, the troops will be stuck in place unable to take a step after piling at the Landing Craft's exit.

text.title: Коротко
lines: The Armory is used to upgrade Troops, Gunboat Weaponry and All Types of Mines.
Troops, Gunboat Weaponry and Mines requires Gold while Proto Troops requires Proto Token
Armory also determines the level of Temporary Gunboat Abilities. They are unlocked at level 8.
Originally Armory also determines the level of Proto Troops, but this was removed with the HQ28 Update. Before that day they were unlocked at Armory level 13.
Upgrading the Armory during an Proto Troop Event didn't have an effect on the levels of the Proto Troops.

text.title: Что меняется с уровнем
lines: Initially, the Armory consists of an open blue Quonset hut with a hatch on the roof where some bullets protrude from it, a pair of wooden steps out front. Several crates of ammunition are visible to the side, as well as a motor. The motor's pistons move while the Armory is upgrading something.

At level 3, the Armory gains a ventilated roof, windows with metal coverings, as well as a stone floor with linings. The roof is much smoother, and several bullets are scattered on the ground near it.
At level 4, the Armory's vent on its roof turns into a ventilation fan.
At level 5, the Armory gains a new metal entrance with closed metal doors and a small metallic ramp.

At level 8, the Armory gains a new metal extension to its right, where several green missiles packed into a cart, apparently that of the Barrage, protrude from it. The crates of ammunition are moved towards the front of the Armory, and the base of the Armory's entrance is reinforced with steel footings. There is also a caution design found just before the metal doors.
At level 14, the Armory gains an extension to the roof where several blue portions appear on top of the original roof.

At level 21, the Armory is overhauled. The entrance appears to have changed from a metal door to metal shutters. The crates containing ammunition and Barrage missiles, as well as the motor are removed. The front is reinforced with some pins, there are two vents and two hatches on the roof of the Armory, and the side that once housed ammunition gains caution designs on its edge. When the Armory is upgrading something, the hatches open to reveal what appears to be spinning gears, and a light is visible from the opening.

At level 22, two stacks, each containing a metal grate and two blue exit tubes, are added on top of the existing vents. A conveyor belt is now added to the opening, though it is inanimate. A crate of ammunition is added outside the Armory.

text.title: Интересное
lines: In the beta version, this building was known as the Combat Academy.

When a Troop upgrade finishes while the player's Landing Craft are loaded with the said troop, several of them will get out of the Landing Craft and walk across the island and back onto the Landing Craft.
There's an achievement which is called Outfitter that gives a total of 60 diamonds upon finishing 235 Armory upgrades.

text.title: Общая информация
lines: The Sculptor is unlocked at Headquarters Level 5 and is used to create special Statues.
There are 4 types of statues: Life, Ice, Magma, and Dark.
Statues provide bonuses to different aspects of the game, such as increasing Building health, Troop damage, Gunboat energy, and Resource production.
You cannot choose the type of bonus the statues will give you, as it is randomized. The bonus value itself cannot be chosen either.
Idol statues can be salvaged for 1 Shard.
Guardian statues can be salvaged for 1 Crystal.
Masterpiece statues can be salvaged for 7 Power Powder.
Each time the Sculptor is upgraded, one unit Power Powder is rewarded.

It is possible to obtain Power Stones and keep them before you have built the Sculptor. Any Power Stones you get are stored on your base. You will not be able to view how many Power Stones you have until the Sculptor is built.
The higher the level of the Sculptor, the more statues can be deployed.
Statues cannot be made while the Sculptor is upgrading.
Likewise, the Sculptor cannot be upgraded while a Statue is being constructed.

text.title: Что меняется с уровнем
lines: Initially, the Sculptor consists of a stone platform and a wooden workbench with tools supposedly used to sculpt statues. There are several short pillars and a short turquoise-colored wall connects these pillars. Life stones are outside the building.

At level 2, the pillars of the Sculptor become much taller, becoming pillars that curve inward, and a turquoise colored wall connects these pillars. A wooden table that holds the life stones appears outside the Sculptor.

At level 3, these walls connecting the pillars turn darker and become taller. A second workbench is added to the Sculptor, and the wooden table outside is extended and now has Magma Power Stones on it.
At level 4, some of the pillars grow taller and more pointed. The table outside of the sculptor now has Ice Power Stones on it. More tools are added onto the second workbench.

At level 5, the Sculptor turns into a hut with an open roof. The roof is turquoise and a red carpet appears at the Sculptor's entrance. The table outside of the sculptor now has all four Power Stone elements on it.

text.title: Интересное
lines: During upgrades, the Statue stored inside the Sculptor will not be visible until its conclusion or cancellation. Statue inside Sculptor
All statues appear as an Idol without a ponytail regardless of its attributes.
The sculptor himself appears to recycle the Warrior's model.
Although the game claims the sculptor cleans up his workshop during upgrades, the building itself does not have a unique upgrade animation or sprite.
Despite the fact that the Statues seem to consist of stone, the Sculptor does not require stone to create them.
The Sculptor is the building that grants the most Experience from a single upgrade, with 110.

text.title: Общая информация
lines: The Vault protects a portion of all Gold, Wood, Stone and Iron from being lost when an enemy player manages to successfully destroy the Headquarters in an attack. Tapping their resource bars will reveal the amount of resources that are under its protection should the base fall.
Everything inside the Vault itself will never be lost to enemy players. They will go in the Vault before any other storage facility.

The Vault's protection percentage applies not only for storages but also uncollected ones on resource production buildings under its owner's influence. This includes the Residences, Sawmill, Quarry, and Iron Mine.
The Vault does not protect Victory Point/Operation Rewards and Submarine treasures until they enter storage, as they cannot be lost in attacks until then.
However, it is possible to lose Wood, Stone and Iron from Resource Boats if one or more owned Resource Bases are taken over by enemy players. See here for more information.

Although the Vault's protected resource amounts are not shown in the resource bar tooltip while it is being upgraded, the vault still functions as normal. This is mentioned in one loading screen hint.

text.title: Что меняется с уровнем
lines: Initially, the Vault is a door locked with a wooden bar leading underground, covered by blue wooden planks. It is reinforced by some sandbags on either side of it, as well as the rear.
At level 2, the roof of the Vault gains two additional wooden strips, with screws to hold them in place. The Vault is further reinforced with two more sandbags, one on each side of the Vault.
At level 4, the roof changes to a corrugated iron material. Some sandbags are removed on each side.
At level 5, the surroundings of the Vault are fortified with finer stone.
At level 6, the wood structure is replaced with stone. The wooden door becomes a more solidified wood, with iron edges and a black iron bar.
At level 8, the Vault gains two metal doors with individual handles. The roof is now made of smooth iron.
At level 9, the door changes to a spinning, watertight door.
At level 10, the outer stone is reinforced with iron braces at the corners.
At level 13, the Vault is now a top-opening spinning iron door on top of a stone platform. The door is also surrounded by smooth iron.
At level 14, the upper door plating underneath the valve is reinforced with a tougher black iron.
At level 15, the entire vault door is fortified with a tougher black iron.
The Vault's protection percentage and storage capacity increases with each upgrade.

text.title: Интересное
lines: The Vault is the only permanent building which has a description that changes with every upgrade, as each increases its resource protection percentage.

With all Resource Storages maxed out and filled to the brim, and a maxed out Vault, the defender will lose 1,468,000 Gold, 1,468,000 Wood, 1,308,000 Stone and 1,308,000 Iron if invaded. Those values don't include production buildings.
By using a maxed out Insurance those losses can further be reduced down to 367,000 Gold, 367,000 Wood, 327,000 Stone and 327,000 Iron. This has no effect on the resources earned by the attacker.

text.title: Коротко
lines: The Residence constantly produces Gold, except during upgrades or when it is full.
The capacity and production rate of a Residence depends on its level.
Gold is used for:
Upgrading your Troops, Heroes, Mines, Boom Mines, Shock Mines and Gunboat Weaponry.
Training and loading Troops on Landing Crafts.
Initiating Attacks (i.e. Against Mercenary, Blackguard, and Resource Bases, Operations, Mega Crab, Mega Turtle, War and the Hammerman Strikes Back Event)
Unlocking regions in the Archipelago.
Going on Submarine dives.
Removing Obstacles.
Uncollected Resources within your Residences can be stolen by attackers. The Vault protects the same percentage of uncollected Resources as Resources in storages.

text.title: Что меняется с уровнем
lines: Initially, the Residence is a blue tent with a flag.
At level 2, the Residence gains some wood planks at the side and a chimney.
At level 3, the Residence becomes a wooden house with a blue roof. The planks are removed and the flag is moved to the side.
At level 4, the wood planks return. The chimney grows slightly in size.
At level 5, a room is added to the side. The wood planks again disappear.
At level 6, the Residence is now made of stone with a corrugated blue metal roof. The chimney is now square. The side room now has a window.
At level 7, a crate is seen near the entrance.
At level 8, the chimney changes design.
At level 9, the roof is now rounded and the door becomes yellow metal.
At level 10, two smaller chimneys are attached to the main one. A window is added to the roof.

text.title: Интересное
lines: The Residence owners presumably pay taxes as Gold.
The Residence is the only Resource production building that can be constructed multiple times but cannot be found on Resource Bases.
Smoke periodically floats out of the chimney of the Residence.
Villagers can enter and exit through the door of the Residence.

text.title: Коротко
lines: The Sawmill constantly produces Wood, except when it is being upgraded or when it is full.
The capacity and production rate of a Sawmill depends on its level.
Wood is the most basic construction material used for upgrades or constructions.
Uncollected Resources within your Sawmill can be stolen by attackers. The Vault protects the same percentage of uncollected Resources as Resources in storages.

text.title: Что меняется с уровнем
lines: Initially, the Sawmill is a large battered wooden building with large front doors and a stone floor. There are logs and a cutting stump outside.
At level 2, the Sawmill gains a few wood planks outside it. The missing wooden plank in the roof has been added.
At level 5, the Sawmill gains a large buzzsaw within its interior, and the roof is replaced with a metal one.
At level 6, the Sawmill's roof is more flattened out, the wooden doors disappear and it receives a stone platform with a wall for storing produced wood.
At level 7, the Sawmill gains a second buzzsaw and a metal chimney.
At level 8, the Sawmill's metal floor is lined with hazard tape, a second metal chimney is installed and the roof is reinforced with steel.
At level 9, the twin chimneys on the roof are replaced with four vents protruding from the roof. A small window is added to the front of the dormer.

text.title: Интересное
lines: When your Wood Storage is full, the bubble you click to collect Wood turns red, indicating that you cannot store the additional Wood produced within your Wood Storage.
The Sawmill is the only building where its last upgrade doesn't cost Wood.

The Sawmill is the only resource production building that requires the resource it produces as part of its upgrade cost (although only at Sawmill levels available at Headquarters level 5 and below, when Wood is the only resource production building unlocked).

The Sawmill, along with the Gunboat and the Headquarters, are the only three buildings that can't be bought from the shop (and thus don't have an initial build cost), as you can only have one of them each, and you start the game with these three already built.
The Sawmill is the only resource producer that can be seen filling up. The platform by the stone wall at Levels 6 and up fills up in a similar manner to Wood Storages.
The early Sawmill levels have stone in them, but Stone is not required to upgrade it.
Similarly, Sawmills at levels 5-6 have a metal roof, but Iron is not required.
At level 7 and above, smoke periodically floats out of the metal chimney.

text.title: Коротко
lines: The Quarry is unlocked at Headquarters level 2.
The Quarry constantly produces Stone, unless it is being upgraded or is full.
The capacity and production rate of a Quarry depends on its level.
Stone is a more advanced resource than Wood, and is mainly used in upgrades or constructions.
Uncollected Resources within your Quarry can be stolen by attackers. The Vault protects the same percentage of uncollected Resources as Resources in storage.

text.title: Что меняется с уровнем
lines: Initially, the Quarry consists of a machine comprised of wheels and pulleys, with a metal box containing a wedge that picks down at a shallow hole in the ground.
At level 2, the machine gains a corrugated metal roof, above the wheels.
At level 3, the box changes color. The wedge it contains is now marked with hazard tape.

At level 4, the roof gains a small metal chimney, and the box containing the wedge changes once again, being marked at the bottom with hazard tape. The hole is now slightly deeper, and the wedge now strikes in the middle of two blocks of stone.
At level 5, the Quarry consists of a large drill on a chute. The hole is deep enough that the bottom cannot be seen.

text.title: Интересное
lines: When your Stone Storage is full, the bubble you click to collect Stone turns red, indicating that you can't store the produced Stone within your Stone Storage.
The drill on levels 5-10 is likely held by electromagnets.
The Quarry was originally unlocked at HQ level 7.

text.title: Коротко
lines: The Iron Mine is unlocked at Headquarters level 3.
The Iron Mine constantly produces Iron, except when it is being upgraded or full.
The capacity and production rate of an Iron Mine depends on its level.
Iron is the most advanced resource used for upgrades and construction.
Uncollected Resources within your Iron Mine can be stolen by attackers. The Vault protects the same percentage of uncollected resources as resources in storage.

text.title: Что меняется с уровнем
lines: Initially, the Iron Mine consists of a stone hill with little bits of iron protruding from it. A blue wooden roof is above the entrance to the hill itself. There is a mine cart track going into the tunnel, and next to it is a metal bucket with melted iron that pours it into ingots molds.

At level 2, the top of the stone hill is covered by a room and a flight of stairs that lead to it appears. A barrel is found outside the tunnel. The roof's supports become stone and are now corrugated metal.
At level 3, the room above the tunnel is extended, and it gains a second barrel outside the tunnel.

At level 5, the Iron Mine gains a new roof and a flat roof covers the track from the curve onward. The barrels are moved to the metal bucket, and the metal bucket gains two tubes behind it. The barrier at the end of the line is now made out of smooth stone instead of wood.

At level 9, the stone hill is now completely gone. The roof is once again remade, and the flat roof now becomes part of the building. The metal bucket becomes its own separate building and has a conveyor belt to receive the iron from the mine cart. A third tank is added beside the belt. The building in which the iron is processed gains two tubes on top on it, and there are some pipes connecting the building and the iron processor. The barrier is now made out of steel with a trapezoidal design, completed with hazard tape at the end. The minecart also becomes metal with a blue stripe.

text.title: Интересное
lines: When your Iron Storage is full, the bubble you click to collect Iron turns red, indicating that you can't store the produced iron within your Iron Storage.

The Iron Mine is currently the only building whose upgrade costs (except the initial build cost) don't follow the resource ratio of the corresponding Headquarters level (the Sawmill and the Quarry still follow the ratio, only with their own resources removed). For example, upgrading to level 8 costs 1,860,000 wood and 1,860,000 stone, but according to the normal ratio, a building level unlocked at HQ level 17 which costs 1,860,000 wood should cost 1,530,000 stone.
Oddly, Villagers carry Iron to the Iron Mine when it is under construction or being upgraded, despite the fact that Iron is never required to upgrade the Iron Mine.
Villagers will also carry iron to a building being upgraded regardless of whether or not it requires iron to upgrade.
The Iron Mine was originally unlocked at HQ level 10.

text.title: Коротко
lines: The more you upgrade the Radar, the more areas you can explore.
After you've upgraded the Radar, you can unlock new regions of the Archipelago with Gold.
The higher the Radar level required to unlock the area, the more expensive the region will be. Larger areas are more expensive to explore as well.
Read about different island types and other points of interest on the Archipelago page.
Upgrading your Radar and then clearing the concealed cloudy regions also increases the cap on the amount of opponents that you can have on your Archipelago at a time.
Invasion information can be found on the Radar info screen at level 6 and beyond.
Upgrading your Radar and then clearing the cloudy regions also increases the number of player's maps that you appear on as a base that can be attacked.

Victory Points also play a small role in the number of player's maps that you appear on, but one's radar level is the most important factor until one reaches 600 Victory Points, when Victory Points become the biggest factor.

text.title: Что меняется с уровнем
lines: Initially, the Radar is simply a dome-shaped receiver that is in a pit bordered by planks of wood.
At level 2, the Radar gains sandbags on the border of its pit. The base changes slightly.
At level 6, the Radar's wooden fence is replaced with a stone base and a metal cabin with windows.

At level 9, the Radar undergoes a complete redesign. The receiver system is changed from a parabolic dish to a tri-fold receiver. The base is also all metal, with a door and room built into it, plus some sandbags. The base also has a side room. The side of the Radar has a metal ladder to reach the receiver. Antennas are also added in the back.

text.title: Интересное
lines: If you have too many unexplored regions, not every region that your Radar level allows you to have will be available for exploration. As you clear more regions, you will be able to clear the newer ones.

It is possible to have some unexplored regions in the map entirely surrounded by explored regions, but never if all explorable regions for any given Radar Level are researched before the Radar is upgraded. For this to happen an area needs to stay unexplored for several Radar levels, until all areas around it can be bought, This does not work for all areas, especially external ones, as areas beyon the Radar's level cap are permanently clouded.
In unexplored regions, Resource Bases, Hammerman's HQs, and transmission towers with active Hero distress signals are visible through the clouds.
Originally only the closest ones could be seen through the clouds; new players can now see them all from the very beginning.

The maximum level of Radar you are allowed to upgrade it to at a particular HQ level is equal to the said HQ level from 1 to 20, and it is one of two buildings to share this trait, the Landing Craft is the other.
To upgrade Headquarters to level 4, you must have Radar level 1. Similarly, to upgrade Headquarters to level 5, your Radar must be upgraded to level 2.
The Radar is the only building to have a palindromic name.

text.title: Коротко
lines: The Weapon Lab is used to build Prototype Defenses.
It is unlocked upon reaching Headquarters level 15.
Upgrading the Weapon Lab allows you to place more powerful and more than one Prototype Defense.
The Weapon Lab cannot be upgraded while a Prototype Defense is being made and vice versa.
Building the Weapon Lab was a perquisite for the Hammerman Strikes Back event.

text.title: Что меняется с уровнем
lines: Initially, the Weapon Lab is a large concrete semicircular structure on a larger circular base. The top is covered by heavy blue plating. A female villager in a lab coat and protective goggles stands next to the lab.
At level 2, the Weapon Lab gains a small blue overhang on the far back. The concrete base is outlined with blue plating.

At level 3, the rest of the concrete base is filled in with another semicircular structure. In the middle is a round metal balcony with a circular warning tape design in the middle. A ladder is added.
At level 4, the blue overhang gains a great deal of bulk, and now has a fan on the top.

At level 5, the blue overhang grows taller and has a drill-like structure on one side. There is a large amount of wire coiled around the place where the semicircular structures do not meet. A warning-tape design is marked on the front of the Lab.

text.title: Интересное
lines: The Weapon Lab and the Engraver are the only buildings whose build/upgrade costs unlocked at a certain Headquarters level exceed the cost to upgrade the Headquarters to the next level.

The Weapon Lab used to reach level 2, 3, 4 and 5 at Headquarters level 16, 17, 18 and 19 respectively (basically 1 upgrade per Headquarters level instead of the current 2 Headquarters levels per Weapon Lab upgrade.

Differently from Statues boosted by Power Powder, if a Prototype defense's timer reaches 0 mid attack, it will be destroyed immediately, regardless of health. Any effect they had on the field, such as Headquarters' Shield for Shield Generators, Sky Shield's air Shield, and damage amplification from Damage Amplifier will be removed immediately.
When watching a replay any Prototype will show the remaining time at the time the attack took place, and the countown will be updated "in real time".

It is currently not known what happens in the case where multiple Shield Generators protect the Headuarters, the Shield is already damaged, and one of the Shield Generators expires. (Example, 2 Shield Generators, Shield at 60%, and one of the Shield Generators expires. Will the Headquarters remain with 30% Shield, 10% Shield, or 60% shield, but halved health?)

When a Prototype Defense's construction is complete, it will be covered by a brown tarp, so players visiting your base will not be able to see which Prototype Defense you have ready. They'll just know you have a replacement when the original expires.
Despite the fact that Prototype Defenses are unstable, they can be stored in the Weapon Lab indefinitely.
There's an achievement which is called Tinkerer that gives a total of 60 diamonds upon using a total of 960 Prototype Modules in the Weapon Lab.

The Weapon Lab only enables building prototype defenses of higher marks up until level 6. Levels 7 to 8 do not provide any higher mark upgrades, and level 6 mainly acts as a barrier from immediately unlocking the 4th prototype defense at level 7.
Originally, all prototype defenses could be upgraded to Mark III at level 5. This was changed in the June 2025 update.

Originally prototypes across all tiers used to last exactly 7 days, but this was changed to 5 days for Mark I, and 9 days for Mark III at a certain update, to make highly expensive Mark III Prototypes last longer than their cheaper Mark I and II variants. This was then changed again to make Mark I Prototypes last 10 days, Mark II 8 days and Mark III 6 days. This update also reworked Module cost for Prototypes, going from 6 to 9 Modules for Mark I Prototypes, and from 18 to 15 Modules for Mark III Prototypes.

This basically means that Mark I prototypes became 40% more expensive than original after the 1st update, but are currently "only 5% more expensive than the original cost", Mark II Prototypes remained unchanged after the 1st patch, but became 14.29% less expensive after the 2nd update, and Mark III Prototypes became 28.57% cheaper to run than original after the 1st update, but the 2nd update made Mark III Prototypes only 2.86% cheaper than their original version.

Another way to visualize prototype cost through the years would be: 0.857 Modules/day for Mark I, 1.714 Modules day for Mark II and 2.571 Modules/day for the original version of the prototypes; at the second version Mark I cost increased to 1.2 Modules/day, and Mark III cost decreased to 2 Modules/day; In the final and current version of the game Mark I prototypes cost 0.9 Modules/day, Mark II cost 1.5 Modules/day and Mark III cost 2.5 Modules a day.

This basically means that to keep 4 Mark III Prototypes running all the time you need to earn at least 10 modules/day. This price increases to 12.5 Modules/day if you also have the Engraving Tinkering.

text.title: Коротко
lines: The Proto Troop Workshop is a support building unlocked at Headquarters level 11.

The Proto Troop Workshop can produce and store Proto Troops for use in attacks. Upgrading the Proto Troop Workshop unlocks: more troop training slots, more squad storage, and more Proto troop offerings. Troop availability changes weekly.
Proto Troops are always consumed upon deployment, and therefore can never be reused, nor could they be garrisoned in a Bunker. However, they will not expire before then.
Since October 2025, the Proto Troop Workshop may also upgrade Proto Troops. Upgrading blocks it from training anymore troops, and vice versa.
With the same update, they introduced temporary access to locked Procurement slots, which cost 100, 200, or 400 depending on the slot. Access will be removed as soon as the next Proto Cycle arrives.

text.title: Что меняется с уровнем
lines: The Proto Troop Workshop has no upgrade differences. It has a steel base with multiple appendages, a ladder to the front, a vent with a dark grey cable to its left and another massive, steel pipe to the right. The topside, divided into two sections is mostly team-colored. The lower side contains a massive, cylindrical access marked by hazard tapes near both ends, surrounded by three steel railings. It is overshadowed by a steel scaffold that supports a team-colored motor with steel gears and vents, attached to a grey belt (marked by hazard tape) and messy dark cables. Suspended beneath is a rudimentary retractable tesla coil. The taller side has a side-mounted vent, a gear, a roof vent and a hazard-marked turbine. Both the turbine and roof vent are linked directly to the structure through thick steel pipes.

It’s possible to have more Proto Troops than the maximum storage capacity allows by loading them onto the Landing Crafts, training new ones in the Workshop, and then swapping the troops on the Landing Crafts.

text.title: Общая информация
lines: The Submarine is an aquatic support structure similar to the Gunboat and Landing Craft.
It is unlocked upon reaching Headquarters level 9.
It can be sent on missions for deep sea treasure at dive locations (yellow buoys with red flags. See image to the right) to uncover large amounts of Resources, Power Stones, and diamonds.
Every dive costs a certain amount of gold.
The deeper the treasure, the longer and costlier it is to dive, but the better the rewards you will get.
The shortest dive time is 6 hours, while the longest can be more than 2 days.
To uncover dive locations, a level 5 Radar is required. You can have up to 3 open dive locations.
Over time, you will use up your dives and your number of open dive locations will diminish.

The fewer open dive locations you have on your map, the more likely it is that a new dive location will appear. This chance is relatively low, however, and it may take several days for a new dive location to appear.
Your map has a 16 possible dive locations that will appear and re-appear over time (See map below).
Each time a dive location appears it will offer different rewards and dive times. The deepest dive offered at a dive location may be less than its maximum possible depth.

text.title: Что меняется с уровнем
lines: The Submarine has no visual difference between upgrades. It is a bright yellow marine craft with black highlights and windows, covered with metal plates. There is a large dome glass window at the front of the craft, and a smaller one on top. There is a hatch at the top, and silver rails on both sides, with a propeller on the back. Buoyant floats are also attached at the bottom of the submarine.
Each level increases the Submarine's maximum dive depth by 100m.

text.title: Интересное
lines: In the past, Submarine dive timers could not be skipped with diamonds or Time Savers.
You can now speed up a dive with diamonds and time savers, as of the September update.
The yellow color of the submarine may be a reference to the Beatles' song "Yellow Submarine".
There's an achievement which is called Submariner that gives a total of 60 diamonds upon diving for treasure 500 times.
The northern part of the Archipelago is filled with Ice Islands. Dive locations in this area are highly likely to give Ice Power Stones.

text.title: Коротко
lines: The Gold Storage is used to store Gold.
Gold is used in upgrading troops, Gunboat Weaponry, Mines, Boom Mines, exploring the Archipelago, training troops, starting Submarine dives, and starting an attack.

Unlike some other real-time strategy games like Clash Of Clans, if this building is destroyed during a battle, the attacker does not necessarily gain some of the Resources in it. The only way Resources can be taken from it is if the attacker destroys the Headquarters.

text.title: Что меняется с уровнем
lines: Initially, the Gold Storage is a wooden box with a wooden padlock on the front, and gold coins are spilling out of it. The box is resting on three wooden planks and the side has a sign with a yellow dollar symbol on it.
At level 2, the Gold Storage gains wooden supports, reinforced corners, and an extra piece of timber underneath. There are more coins spilling out of the front.
At level 4, the reinforced corners turn gray, and even more coins are spilling out.
At level 6, the Gold Storage becomes a metal box with stone edges, with even more coins spilling out. The padlock's chain gains a color similar to the metal parts of the building.
At level 8, the sides are a patchy gold-colored metal, and the front and back edges are reinforced with more stone. The base is also made completely out of stone, and the padlock turns golden.
At level 10, the Gold Storage is made completely out of golden-colored metal with a stone base. It changes to resemble a more vault-like structure with a circular door.

text.title: Интересное
lines: You do not need to have the necessary level of Gold Storage for upgrades if you buy Gold with Diamonds, or obtain excess Gold through the Trader.

The Gold Storage and Headquarters are the only storage buildings that do not fill up visually. The Wood Storage visually fills up with planks; the Stone Storage visually fills up with stones; and the Iron Storage fills up with iron ingots.
There's an achievement which is called War Chest that gives a total of 60 diamonds upon upgrading one Gold Storage to level 10.

The storage capacity for any resource storage building is increased at an increasing rate on each upgrade, with the only exception being levels 12 and 13, which only increases the capacity by 500,000 compared to the previous upgrades offering an increase by 1,000,000.

lines: The Stone Storage is unlocked at Headquarters level 3.

text.title: Общая информация
lines: The Statue Storage is a Support Building used to store Statues and is unlocked at Headquarters Level 13.
Only newly sculpted Statues that have NOT been deployed can be placed in the Statue Storage.
Statues that are placed in the Statue Storage do not boost any stats. The Statue must be taken out of the Storage and deployed on the player's base in order to have an effect.
Once deployed, a Statue cannot be placed back in the Statue Storage.
A Statue in the Statue Storage can be salvaged normally while inside the storage, freeing up space for any future statues.

text.title: Что меняется с уровнем
lines: Initially, the Statue Storage is a small hut with blue, cloth-like walls and tan pillars. The floor is made of rough stone tiles, and there are numerous spikes sticking out of the pillars, and a pile of rope on the left corner.
At level 2, the walls of the Statue Storage are extended to form a roof. A white design is seen on the walls.
At level 3, the walls and roof of the Statue Storage gain white trims.
At level 4, the floor of the Statue Storage is replaced by a long woven wood carpet.
At level 5, a small table with a light blue tablecloth is placed inside the Statue Storage. A pulley with some rope is attached to the back.

text.title: Интересное
lines: Like the Sculptor, Fragments can be toggled in the Statue Storage from the Power Stone display and converted into Shards.
The Statue Storage has the lowest total xp reward for building and upgrading, with a measly total of only 83 xp.

text.title: Коротко
lines: You can build the Engraver after reaching Headquarter Level 27.
The Engraver is used to unlock and upgrade powerful Engravings.
Combat Engravings will be unlocked with Level 1 and Defense Engravings with Level 2.
You can activate an engraving instantly with 1 Power Powder for a duration of 12 hours for combat, and 36 hours for defense.
Active Engravings do not affect Warships.

text.title: Интересное
lines: The Engraver and the Proto Troop Workshop are the only structure without any upgrade differences for all levels.
Previously, activating an engraving was permanent and required 7 super powders for instant activation or 4 super powders and a wait time of 12 hours.
With 10 million building resources for each, the Engraver is the most expensive building in the game.
The Engraver has also the highest upgrade cost in the game, with 12 million building resources of each type for level 2 and 14 million of each type for level 3.
Adrenaline was the first Engraving introduced to Warships at Season 82.
The Engraver has the lowest maximum HP out of all player buildings.
Devs builds have a limit of 99 999 Research Tokens, 99 000 more than the in game cap, as can be seen from the screenshots in Engraving Research.
Troops inside the Bunker or spawned from Critter Launcher, Extra Garrison, and Mind Control are affected by Combat Engravings, even if they defend the Base.
